key_insight: Semi-supervised learning with ensemble consensus improves molecular graph prediction without needing label-preserving augmentations, and can make a single model outperform a traditionally trained ensemble.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to leverage abundant unlabeled molecular data to improve prediction accuracy, robustness, and calibration in drug discovery and materials informatics workflows.
method: Train graph neural networks with an ensemble consensus objective on labeled and unlabeled molecular graphs.
Use consensus among ensemble members as a learning signal instead of relying on handcrafted molecular augmentations.
Distill ensemble behavior into individual models to gain ensemble-like benefits at lower inference cost.
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated across diverse molecular datasets, task types, and GNN architectures, and the abstract reports improved predictive accuracy and reduced calibration error in almost all cases.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on a suitable ensemble-consensus training setup, so added training complexity and compute overhead may be a practical concern.
paper_title: Semi-Supervised Learning for Molecular Graphs via Ensemble Consensus
